citations.quote: CE is a program offered between a public high school and a participating Utah System of Higher Education (USHE) institution. Challenging, college-level courses are offered to high school students.
Public school students in grades 9, 10, 11, or 12.
Students must complete Secondary Math I, II, and III with a “C” average or better course grade in all three classes to enroll in a CE mathematics course.
CE credits and grades will be posted on a student’s high school transcript and count toward the high school GPA.
A student may be charged partial tuition, up to $30 per credit hour, for each concurrent enrollment course for which the student receives college credit.
The credit, for high school graduation purposes, is guaranteed (if the student successfully earns it), however, scholarship and college/university eligibility may be affected.
the course taken will be recorded in the student's high school transcript, so grades earned will be included in the student's 9th grade GPA.
"Dual enrollment student" means a student who is enrolled simultaneously in: (a) a private school or home school; and (b) a public school.

A 7th or 8th grade student may earn credit for a mathematics foundation course before 9th grade, consistent with the student's Plan for College and Career Readiness if: (a) the student is identified as gifted in mathematics in accordance with the procedures outlined in Rule R277-707;

(b) the student is enrolled at a middle school or junior high school and a high school; (c) the student qualifies for promotion one or two grade levels above the student's age group and is placed in 9th grade; or
(d) the student takes the Board competency test in the summer before 9th grade and earns high school graduation credit for the course.
A student who successfully completes a mathematics foundation course before 9th grade shall earn 3.0 units of additional mathematics credit by:
Students in grades 6-12 enrolled in a Utah public school are eligible for participation.

options.note: College classes for high school and college credit in grades 9-12. They can cost up to $30 a credit hour, and often less. Grades go on your high school and college transcripts. CE math needs a C average or better in Secondary Math I, II and III.
Online classes for Utah public school students in grades 6-12, useful when your school doesn't offer a class.

middleSchoolMath.text: In Utah, a 7th or 8th grader can earn high school math credit only if identified as gifted in math, enrolled at both a middle or junior high school and a high school, promoted to 9th grade, or by passing the state's test the summer before 9th grade.

A math class passed before 9th grade still leaves 3 more math credits to earn in high school, and its grade goes into your 9th-grade GPA. It may affect scholarship or college eligibility, so check first.

terms.meaning: Utah's name for college classes you take in high school for both high school and college credit.
In Utah this means a private school or home school student who also takes some classes at a public school. It isn't college credit.
